title: CDL Hazmat placarding practice questions
description: Free CDL Hazmat placarding practice questions on 49 CFR 172 Subpart F. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Which of these does 172.500(b) list among the materials the placarding subpart does not apply to?

options.A: Combustible liquids in cargo tanks
options.B: Division 2.3 gases in non-bulk cylinders
options.C: Combustible liquids in non-bulk packagings
options.D: Class 8 materials in bulk packagings

questions.explanation: 172.500(b) states that the subpart does not apply to "(5) Combustible liquids in non-bulk packagings." The exception is limited to non-bulk packagings.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.500, Applicability of placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.500(b)(2), which condition takes hazardous materials authorized to be offered as a limited quantity outside the placarding subpart?

options.A: When identified as such on a shipping paper in accordance with 172.203(b) or when marked as such in accordance with 172.315
options.B: Only when the vehicle carries less than 454 kg (1,001 pounds) of them
options.C: Only when they move by rail
options.D: Only when the carrier's vehicle is already placarded

questions.explanation: The subpart does not apply to limited quantity materials "when identified as such on a shipping paper in accordance with § 172.203(b) or when marked as such in accordance with § 172.315."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.500, Applicability of placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.506(a), in which situation does the person offering a hazardous material to a motor carrier by highway not have to provide the required placards?

options.A: When the driver holds a hazardous materials endorsement
options.B: When the material is loaded at the carrier's own terminal
options.C: When the shipment goes to a single consignee
options.D: When the carrier's motor vehicle is already placarded for the material as required by the subpart

questions.explanation: The offeror "shall provide to the motor carrier the required placards for the material being offered prior to or at the same time the material is offered for transportation, unless the carrier's motor vehicle is already placarded for the material as required by this subpart."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.506, Providing and affixing placards: Highway (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.507(b), where may a nurse tank meeting 173.315(m) go without a placard?

options.A: On any side facing the road shoulder
options.B: On an end containing valves, fittings, regulators or gauges, when those appurtenances prevent the markings and placard from being properly placed and visible
options.C: On every side, while the tank is on a farm
options.D: On the top, when a placard holder is used

questions.explanation: A nurse tank "is not required to be placarded on an end containing valves, fittings, regulators or gauges when those appurtenances prevent the markings and placard from being properly placed and visible."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.507, Special placarding provisions: Highway (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Hazardous materials are offered for transportation not involving air transportation in a freight container with a capacity of less than 640 cubic feet, and the container is not placarded. What does 172.512(b)(2) require?

options.A: The freight container must display one DANGEROUS placard on each end
options.B: The freight container must be labeled in accordance with Subpart E
options.C: The freight container must carry a copy of the shipping paper on its door
options.D: The freight container must be marked "HOT"

questions.explanation: Such a freight container "need not be placarded. However, if not placarded, it must be labeled in accordance with subpart E of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.512, Freight containers and aircraft unit load devices (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which kind of display on a motor vehicle does 172.502(a)(2) prohibit?

options.A: Any sign that shows the motor carrier's name
options.B: Any advertisement placed more than 3 inches from a placard
options.C: Any slogan written in a language other than English
options.D: A sign, advertisement, slogan or device that, by its color, design, shape or content, could be confused with a placard prescribed in the subpart

questions.explanation: No person may display "Any sign, advertisement, slogan (such as “Drive Safely”), or device that, by its color, design, shape or content, could be confused with any placard prescribed in this subpart."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.502, Prohibited and permissive placarding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: General requirements and the placard tables
questions.question: Which Division 6.1 material is listed in Table 1 of 172.504(e)?

options.A: Material poisonous by inhalation
options.B: Packing Group III material
options.C: Material in non-bulk packagings
options.D: Material other than material poisonous by inhalation

questions.explanation: Table 1 lists "6.1 (material poisonous by inhalation (see § 171.8 of this subchapter))", while Table 2 lists "6.1 (other than material poisonous by inhalation)".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: General requirements and the placard tables
questions.question: Which Class 7 entry appears in Table 1 of 172.504(e)?

options.A: Class 7 (Radioactive White I label only)
options.B: Class 7 (Radioactive Yellow II label only)
options.C: Class 7 (Radioactive Yellow III label only)
options.D: Class 7 (any radioactive material in any package)

questions.explanation: The Class 7 row of Table 1 reads "7 (Radioactive Yellow III label only)"; a footnote adds certain other shipments that also require RADIOACTIVE placards.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: The 454 kg exception and empty packages
questions.question: Besides hazardous materials subject to 172.505, what does 172.504(c) leave outside its exception for less than 454 kg (1,001 pounds) of Table 2 materials?

options.A: Non-bulk packages of Class 3 materials
options.B: Bulk packagings
options.C: Freight containers moved by highway
options.D: Shipments moved by rail

questions.explanation: 172.504(c) begins "Except for bulk packagings and hazardous materials subject to § 172.505, when hazardous materials covered by table 2 of this section are transported by highway or rail, placards are not required on—".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: The 454 kg exception and empty packages
questions.question: When working out placarding requirements, how does 172.504(d)(1) treat a non-bulk packaging that contains only the residue of a Table 2 material not subject to 172.505?

options.A: It counts at its full marked capacity
options.B: It counts as 454 kg (1,001 pounds) on its own
options.C: It must be placarded on two opposite sides
options.D: It need not be included in determining placarding requirements

questions.explanation: "Except for hazardous materials subject to § 172.505, a non-bulk packaging that contains only the residue of a hazardous material covered by Table 2 of paragraph (e) of this section need not be included in determining placarding requirements."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.504(b), which load may be placarded with a DANGEROUS placard instead of separate placards?

options.A: A compartmented cargo tank carrying two different Table 2 materials
options.B: A transport vehicle with two or more Table 1 materials
options.C: A transport vehicle with non-bulk packages of two or more categories of hazardous materials that require different Table 2 placards
options.D: A transport vehicle carrying a single Division 2.3 material

questions.explanation: A transport vehicle "which contains non-bulk packages with two or more categories of hazardous materials that require different placards specified in table 2 of paragraph (e) of this section may be placarded with a DANGEROUS placard".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A transport vehicle carrying mixed non-bulk Table 2 materials is placarded DANGEROUS. Under 172.504(b), what makes the Table 2 placard for one category of material required on it?

options.A: 1,000 kg (2,205 pounds) aggregate gross weight or more of that category loaded at one loading facility
options.B: 454 kg (1,001 pounds) of that category loaded anywhere during the trip
options.C: Any quantity of that category
options.D: That category making up more than half of the load's weight

questions.explanation: "However, when 1,000 kg (2,205 pounds) aggregate gross weight or more of one category of material is loaded therein at one loading facility ... the placard specified in table 2 ... for that category must be applied."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A transport vehicle carries a non-flammable gas together with a flammable gas and is placarded FLAMMABLE GAS as required. What does 172.504(f)(3) say about the NON-FLAMMABLE GAS placard?

options.A: It must also be displayed on each side and each end
options.B: It is not required
options.C: It must replace the FLAMMABLE GAS placard on the front
options.D: It must be displayed on the rear only

questions.explanation: "A NON-FLAMMABLE GAS placard is not required on a transport vehicle which contains nonflammable gas if the transport vehicle also contains flammable gas or oxygen and it is placarded with FLAMMABLE GAS or OXYGEN placards, as required."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For domestic transportation, a CLASS 9 placard is not required. What does 172.504(f)(9) still require for a bulk packaging of a Class 9 material?

options.A: It must display a DANGEROUS placard on each end
options.B: It must display CLASS 9 placards on each side and each end
options.C: It must carry a POISON placard on two opposite sides
options.D: It must be marked with the appropriate identification number on a CLASS 9 placard, an orange panel, or a white square-on-point display configuration

questions.explanation: "However, a bulk packaging must be marked with the appropriate identification number on a CLASS 9 placard, an orange panel, or a white square-on-point display configuration as required by subpart D of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.504, General placarding requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A transport vehicle contains a material with a subsidiary hazard of being dangerous when wet, as defined in 173.124. What does 172.505(c) require?

options.A: DANGEROUS WHEN WET placards on each side and each end, in addition to the placards required by 172.504
options.B: DANGEROUS WHEN WET placards only when 454 kg (1,001 pounds) or more is loaded
options.C: DANGEROUS WHEN WET placards in place of the placards required by 172.504
options.D: Labels on the packages only, with no subsidiary placard

questions.explanation: Such a vehicle "shall be placarded with DANGEROUS WHEN WET placards, on each side and each end, in addition to the placards required by § 172.504."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.505, Placarding for subsidiary hazards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A bulk packaging that had to be placarded while it held a hazardous material is now empty. Which condition in 172.514(b) allows it to no longer be placarded?

options.A: It holds less than 454 kg (1,001 pounds) of residue
options.B: It has been unloaded for more than 24 hours
options.C: It is sufficiently cleaned of residue and purged of vapors to remove any potential hazard
options.D: The driver carries the shipping paper from the last load

questions.explanation: It "must remain placarded when it is emptied, unless it— (1) Is sufficiently cleaned of residue and purged of vapors to remove any potential hazard;" (or meets one of the other listed conditions).

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.514, Bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.514(c)(1), how may a portable tank having a capacity of less than 3,785 L (1,000 gallons) be placarded?

options.A: It needs neither placards nor labels
options.B: Only with a DANGEROUS placard
options.C: On the front end only
options.D: On only two opposite sides or, alternatively, labeled instead of placarded in accordance with Subpart E

questions.explanation: "The following packagings may be placarded on only two opposite sides or, alternatively, may be labeled instead of placarded in accordance with subpart E of this part: (1) A portable tank having a capacity of less than 3,785 L (1,000 gallons)."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.514, Bulk packagings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.516(b), where may the required placarding of the front of a motor vehicle be displayed?

options.A: Only on the front of the cargo body
options.B: On the front of the truck-tractor, instead of or in addition to the front of the cargo body
options.C: Inside the windshield
options.D: On the roof of the cab

questions.explanation: "The required placarding of the front of a motor vehicle may be on the front of a truck-tractor instead of or in addition to the placarding on the front of the cargo body to which a truck-tractor is attached."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.516, Visibility and display of placards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.516(c)(6), who must maintain a placard so that its format, legibility, color and visibility are not substantially reduced by damage, deterioration or dirt?

options.A: The carrier
options.B: The consignee
options.C: The placard manufacturer
options.D: The State that issued the driver's CDL

questions.explanation: Each placard must "Be maintained by the carrier in a condition so that the format, legibility, color, and visibility of the placard will not be substantially reduced due to damage, deterioration, or obscurement by dirt or other matter;".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.516, Visibility and display of placards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 172.542(c), on which placard may the word "GASOLINE" be used in place of the word "FLAMMABLE"?

options.A: A placard on any transport vehicle carrying non-bulk gasoline cans
options.B: A placard on a rail tank car only
options.C: A placard displayed on a cargo tank or a portable tank being used to transport gasoline by highway
options.D: A placard on any vehicle carrying Class 3 material

questions.explanation: "The word “GASOLINE” may be used in place of the word “FLAMMABLE” on a placard that is displayed on a cargo tank or a portable tank being used to transport gasoline by highway."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.542, FLAMMABLE placard (as of Nov 4, 2026)
